newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan cracks down on illegal hard currency trade.
newsitem.headline: Sudan cracks down on illegal hard currency trade.

text.p: Sudan has jailed more than 50 people and closed eight foreign exchange houses in a major crackdown on illegal trade in foreign currency, a privately-owned newspaper said on Saturday.

The daily Alwan said a court set up in August to combat the illegal money trafficking had imposed prison terms ranging from six months to three years for hard currency brokers and sellers of forged money.
Officials have also seized 250 million Sudanese pounds ($172,000) and Saudi riyals since August, the daily said.
Alwan said the measures have boosted the Sudanese pound against the U.S. dollar and Saudi Arabia's riyal, the two most popular foreign currencies traded in the African country.
It said the U.S. dollar has fallen to 1,665 Sudanese pounds from 2,000 pounds on the black market in August.
The riyal also fell in the same period to 440 pounds from 590 in the blackmarket and 388 pounds in exchange houses.
The daily said exchange firms which were closed had violated regulations set up by the central bank, the Bank of Sudan.
The Bank of Sudan had decreed that exchange bureaus must fix rates on a daily basis based on the average of the day before.
It said exchange companies that deal in hard currency must close all their accounts and leave one hard currency account and one local currency account in one branch of a commercial bank.

They were also required to obtain certificates from the Bank of Sudan before making available hard currency to finance imports. Under the new regulations, exchange bureaus are not allowed to make more than two percent profit.
